summary: A riverside Shiva shrine and bathing ghat on the Ahwa–Saputara road — a shady halt where road, river and a small temple meet.
description:
Shivghat is the kind of stop Dang's interior roads offer without announcing: a small Shiva shrine at a river crossing on the Ahwa–Saputara stretch, with stone steps to the water, big shade trees, and — in monsoon — the river running loud enough to make tea taste better at the adjacent stall. Local families treat it as a bathing and picnic ghat; Shravan brings modest devotional traffic.

For travellers it is a fifteen-minute leg-stretch that delivers more atmosphere than several ticketed stops: temple bell, water over rock, forest on both banks. Flow shrinks to pools by late winter.
highlights: Shady tea-stall halt on the Ahwa road

modes.road: On/just off the Ahwa–Saputara road; watch for the small signboard

access.last_mile: Steps from the roadside down to the ghat

visit.notes: Shravan Mondays bring local devotional crowds.

seasonality.notes: The river is the show — monsoon through early winter.

experience.photography_notes: Slow-shutter water frames from the steps in monsoon; shade makes midday workable.

amenities.food: Tea and snack stall in season

warnings: Bathe only at the steps in gentle flow — monsoon current is deceptive

tips: Natural tea-break on the Ahwa–Saputara run — time it that way

seo.meta_description: Shivghat on the Ahwa–Saputara road: riverside shrine, bathing steps and the monsoon halt worth making.
